bottles.name: Espadin Mezcal
bottles.note: Roasted in a stone pit, so the smoke is a method, not a flavouring.

bottles.name: Alpine Amaro
bottles.note: Root, mint and bitterness. Drink it after everything else has failed.

bottles.name: Maraschino Liqueur
bottles.note: Marasca cherry with the stones in. Nothing like the syrup of the same name.

bottles.name: London Dry Gin
bottles.note: Juniper-forward and unambiguous. The gin a Martini was written for.

bottles.name: Orange Curacao
bottles.note: Bitter orange in brandy. The unglamorous third of a Sidecar.

bottles.name: Rhum Agricole Blanc
bottles.note: Pressed cane juice, never molasses. Grassy and faintly saline.

bottles.name: Blanco Tequila
bottles.note: Unaged, additive-free, and tasting of the plant rather than the barrel.

bottles.name: Sweet Vermouth
bottles.note: Keep it in the fridge. Yes, really - it is wine, and it dies in a cupboard.

bottles.name: Single Malt, 10 Years
bottles.note: Orchard fruit, a little malt sweetness, no smoke to argue with.

bottles.name: Reposado Tequila
bottles.note: Eight months in oak. Softer, and it stops fighting the glass.

bottles.name: Dry Vermouth
bottles.note: Alpine and bone-dry. The half of a Martini nobody credits.

bottles.name: Creme de Cassis
bottles.note: Blackcurrant, thick and dark. One bar spoon changes a whole drink.

bottles.name: Straight Rye
bottles.note: Dry, peppery, and the reason a Manhattan has a spine.

bottles.name: Aged Rum, 8 Years
bottles.note: Tropical ageing does in eight years what Scotland needs twenty for.

bottles.name: Small Batch Bourbon
bottles.note: Corn-sweet and vanilla-heavy, with enough oak to stop it being a dessert.

bottles.name: Bitter Aperitivo
bottles.note: Rhubarb and gentian, coloured somewhere between sunset and a warning.

bottles.name: Navy Strength Gin
bottles.note: Overproof, so it survives contact with citrus and ice without going quiet.

bottles.name: Overproof White Rum
bottles.note: Funky, high-ester and unreasonable. Built for tiki and for float.

bottles.name: Barrel-Rested Gin
bottles.note: Six months in oak. Somewhere between a gin and a young whisky, and honest about it.

bottles.name: Peated Single Malt
bottles.note: Coastal and medicinal. Divides a room faster than politics.
